chunks: Al-Sakūnī narrated with his chain of transmission.
That the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم saw a she-camel tied up while its gear was still upon it, and he said:
"Where is its owner? Tell him to prepare tomorrow for dispute."

key_terms.اَلسَّكُونِيُّ: Al-Sakūnī, the narrator transmitting this report
key_terms.اَلنَّبِيَّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.اَلْخُصُومَةِ: dispute or litigation, here referring to reckoning before Allah

ai.seo_question: What does Islam teach about mistreating animals and being held accountable for it on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against neglecting and wronging animals, specifically by leaving a camel restrained with its gear upon it. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم teaches that such oppression is a matter of accountability and dispute on the Day of Judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2490 - Al-Sakuni narrated with his chain of transmission
that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) saw a camel tied up with its gear still on it.
Prophet (sw) said: "Where is its owner? Tell him to prepare for a dispute tomorrow (on the Day of Judgment)."
